items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: And one of them was Bob Newman, a saxophone player. He encouraged me to come to York... As soon as you get there, look me up, I can get you work right away.

ctx.x: I guess you did. When I look at the list of people that you’ve played with and that have played with you it’s pretty darn impressive. You eventually, like a lot of people, moved to New York. Was that specifically for the music?

Yeah it sure was. I had just come out of the Air Force. I had spent two years in the Air Force and I was deciding which coast to go to. I knew I wasn’t going home to the Twin Cities. But I was going to go to either New York or California. And I ran into, well I was stationed in Salt Lake. And the Woody Herman band came through. I met some guys on that band and hung out with them for the couple days they were in town. And they encouraged me. And one of them was Bob Newman, a saxophone player. He encouraged me to…
Wow. He’s a very unique guy.
